comment: This contradicts STT's paper, which says stores that act before retirement 'are defined as transmitters' and that 'loads and stores access memory only if their address argument is untainted'. AMuLeT calls KV3 an implementation bug, and SimSpect's own SPT model has store transmitters, so the sentence describes the STT_6 model rather than SimSpect or STT (whole sentence from 'We \emph{do not} find' should change).
proposed: We do not find STT's tainted-store\,$\to$\,TLB bug: our STT model has only load and branch transmitters, although STT's paper also treats stores that act before retirement as transmitters~\cite[Sec.~6.1]{stt}, so this miss is a gap in our STT model.
evidence: ~/Documents/quail/sources/papers/yu-2019-stt.pdf Sec. 6.1 and Sec. 6.4.2; fu-2025-amulet.pdf Sec. 4.8 (KV3 'root cause is an implementation bug'); STAGE1_alloy/models/SPT_6_oneLP.als:344; STAGE1_alloy/models/STT_6.als:328

anchor: We present a formal language intermediate representation for specifying defenses and proving security properties
comment: Nothing in the repo or the paper proves a security property from a SimSpect specification; the language is only used to enumerate tests. Drop 'proving security properties' unless a proof is added.
proposed: We present a formal language for specifying a defense's leakage rules
evidence: grep for proof work in wiki/, STATUS.md, PAPER_PLAN.md finds none; sections/model.tex and sections/pipeline.tex contain no proof

anchor: and can be used to generate test sets or to prove adherence to a higher level security property.
comment: No proof of adherence exists in the repo. The sentence before it ('precise to the cases blocked by a defense') is also contradicted by documented over-approximations: SPT's operand-based protection set produces the const-address hits (about 99.9% of SPT load hits), and Recon_6's reveal policy is a no-op.
proposed: and is used to generate test sets; using it to prove adherence to a higher-level security property is future work.

anchor: Fig.~\ref{fig:race} shows the race on test inst-047231, on an STT build with \texttt{commitToIEWDelay}~$=4$.
comment: The trace was taken with se_slowcomm.py. That script sets iewToCommitDelay=30, commitToIEWDelay=4, backComSize=forwardComSize=40 and squashWidth=1, with a 150-cycle fnc commit stall, not just commitToIEWDelay=4. The bug folder's minimal reproduction is commitToIEWDelay=3 with squashWidth=8 and the fnc stall off; the Fig. race caption has the same omission.
proposed: Fig.~\ref{fig:race} shows the race on test inst-047231, on STT with slowed squash propagation (\texttt{commitToIEWDelay}~$=4$, \texttt{iewToCommitDelay}~$=30$, \texttt{squashWidth}~$=1$); \texttt{commitToIEWDelay}~$=3$ alone also triggers it.

anchor: only the unresolved-branch stall changes the verdict
comment: The stall sweeps ran before the 2026-10-30 fix to the resolve-stall hook. Its deferred release never woke a sleeping CPU, so stalled runs committed late or froze until the tick cap and were scored as non-hits, and the 27-to-0 drop at s_U >= 50 may be that bug rather than masking. s_R (27 to 22) and the fnc stall (16 to 27) also change the hit count, so 'only s_U changes the verdict' and 'flat plateau' overstate.
evidence: claudelog.md 2026-10-30 resolve-hooks ('Resolve-stall hook froze runs (pre-existing, all 8 builds)'); paper_figures/plans/RESULTS_FIGURES.md §3 fig:timing row; claudelog.md 2026-06-03 05:50; wiki/findings/mdsToRead/NEAR_MISS_BREAKDOWN.md:87

anchor: transmitter out of the window at $\geq50$ cyc), never manufactures one.
comment: The caption has the same problem. The s_U points predate the fix to the resolve-stall hook that froze sleeping CPUs, so 'pushes the transmitter out of the window' and 'never manufactures one' are not established, and 'measured; both bucket-confirmed' does not say that both sweeps are pre-fix.

The taken-mode series (0/0/2/2 per 300) used the old BTB force, which the 2026-10-30 hook audit found wrong on every build (decode-squashed on gem5-22 builds; on older builds the wrong path starts at the label and skips LLVM-hoisted instructions). So the near-zero taken counts may reflect the force rather than STT; re-run taken mode on the fixed harness or drop the series.
evidence: STATUS.md:30; claudelog.md 2026-10-30 resolve-hooks ('Old BTB force wrong'); wiki/findings/mdsToRead/NEAR_MISS_BREAKDOWN.md:88 (frag_d* on /work/stt); wiki/results/PAPER_RESULTS.md §7 table

anchor: Every count in this section is a \emph{confirmed} real leak
comment: Several counts in the section fail this bar. The targeting percentages are static; the SpecLFB hits were scored with SpecLFB's own isUnsafe flag on accesses that hit the cache, not with the packet/store-forward gate; and check_ld's data-obtained gate asks whether any instance at the transmitter's PC ever sent a packet or completed, not whether this instance did inside the window. The bug catalog also still marks the STT race as open and not independently re-verified.
proposed: Each load hit counted here passed the per-transmitter checker on the defense build (a cache packet or a completed store-forward at the transmitter's PC, with the load executing inside the window); static and model-only signals are reported separately
evidence: claudelog.md 2026-11-02 transmission-criteria audit (STAGE3_gem5/check_ld.py:56-75); URGENT_TODO.md DECIDE 'no reported result used the JSON transmission criteria' (check_ld_speclfb.py trusts isUnsafe); wiki/findings/bug/BUGS.md STT race entry (open)

anchor: first speculative load in the LSQ unprotected so that it performs its in-window cache access,
comment: Separate from the pre-fix issue: the counted SpecLFB loads hit a pre-warmed line and installed nothing, and SpecLFB's paper puts leakage through speculative loads that hit the cache outside its scope. After the checker was re-keyed to L1 installs, the earlier hits became no-install. The 2026-10-28 audit also found that when a stall hook opens the window (as in SimSpect's tests), SpecLFB leaves the second speculative load unprotected too, an artifact that 'should not be counted as UV6'.
proposed: first speculative load in the LSQ unprotected, so that it installs a cache line inside the window (counted with the install-keyed check on cache-missing addresses),
evidence: wiki/results/PAPER_RESULTS.md §4 (every xmit load reads prologue-pre-warmed 0x3580, ReadReq hit); claudelog.md 2026-06-03 'CHECKER CHANGE: SpecLFB UV6 leak re-keyed on the actual L1 line-INSTALL'; cheng-2024-speclfb.pdf Sec. 9; wiki/findings/audits/2026-10-28/hooks_speclfb_and_uv6.md:7-21

anchor: xmit's L1D eviction ($\star$) meets InvisiSpec's criterion before xmit is squashed, so the test is reported as a violation.
comment: check_footprint counts a footprint by any squashed instruction younger than lc, not just the transmitter. In this trace seqs 566, 573 (xmit) and 576 all qualify, and the earliest in-window footprint is seq 566's L2 coherence change at cycle 16, so the verdict does not depend on xmit's eviction. The fixture also predates the 2026-10-30 harness fix (5000-cycle resolve stall).
proposed: xmit's L1D eviction ($\star$) is one of the in-window footprints that meet InvisiSpec's criterion (the criterion counts any squashed load younger than lc), so the test is reported as a violation.
evidence: claudelog.md 2026-11-02 'InvisiSpec footprint checker attributes leaks to any squashed load'; paper_figures/plans/fig_e_checkerwindow.md:140,199; URGENT_TODO.md InvisiSpec footprint DECIDE
